notes: Evals for the documentation-propagation phase. Tests the three-signal traversal (browzer mentions reverse, direct-path-refs, concept-level), the legitimate-skip path when no downstream impact exists, the `.updateDocs.patches` shape, and the no-fabrication guard (don't invent doc paths the probes didn't return).

evals.name: three-signals-all-applied
evals.prompt: A TASK changed `packages/core/src/auth/session.ts`. Describe the THREE signals you use to find downstream docs that need updating, in the order you run them.
evals.expected_output: (1) `browzer mentions packages/core/src/auth/session.ts` — graph reverse traversal (File ← RELEVANT_TO ← Entity ← MENTIONS ← Chunk ← HAS_CHUNK ← Document). (2) Direct-path refs — `browzer search` for the literal path string + basename in markdown corpus. (3) Concept-level refs — `browzer search` for high-level concepts cited in the changed code (e.g., 'session refresh', 'JWT verification'). Each signal saves to a temp file and the union becomes the candidate set.

evals.name: legitimate-skipped-when-no-downstream
evals.prompt: A TASK changed only `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The three signals all return zero candidates. What do you write to workflow.json?
evals.expected_output: Step status SKIPPED with `applicability.applicable: false`, `applicability.reason: "no downstream documentation impact (three signals returned zero candidates)"`, `updateDocs.patches: []`. Does NOT fabricate a fake README update or invent CLAUDE.md changes. The legitimate-skip path is what kept S1 in RETRO #2 from being a regression — see the CHANGELOG anchor convention.

evals.name: no-fabricated-doc-paths
evals.prompt: Three signals returned only `apps/api/CLAUDE.md`. The user prompt mentions 'this is also documented in our /docs/auth.md page'. You can't find `/docs/auth.md` via grep, browzer search, or any signal. Do you patch it?
evals.expected_output: No. Don't fabricate paths the probes did not return. Operator references can be wrong (page renamed, deleted, was always aspirational). Surface the discrepancy: 'You mentioned /docs/auth.md but the three signals + grep don't find it. Possible candidates from probes: apps/api/CLAUDE.md. Should I (a) patch the candidate, (b) confirm /docs/auth.md was renamed, (c) skip docs?' Then proceed per operator answer.

assertions.name: asks-operator
assertions.check: output contains 'operator' and ('confirm' or 'ask' or 'should I')

evals.name: patches-shape-on-update-docs-field
evals.prompt: Show the JSONC shape of one entry in `.updateDocs.patches[]` for a CHANGELOG anchor update.
evals.expected_output: `{ path: "docs/CHANGELOG.md", kind: "insert-anchor" | "replace-section" | "append-line", anchor: "<#anchor-id>", oldText: "<verbatim>", newText: "<verbatim>", reason: "<one line>" }`. Each patch is independently apply-able + reversible. The `oldText` field is mandatory for diff verification — patches without it are rejected as ambiguous.
